# ipcalc

This is the ipv6 capable continuation of the subnet calculator from http://jodies.de/ipcalc. 

<pre>
> ipcalc 192.168.1.1/24
Address:   192.168.1.1          11000000.10101000.00000001. 00000001
Netmask:   255.255.255.0 = 24   11111111.11111111.11111111. 00000000
Wildcard:  0.0.0.255            00000000.00000000.00000000. 11111111
=>
Network:   192.168.1.0/24       11000000.10101000.00000001. 00000000
HostMin:   192.168.1.1          11000000.10101000.00000001. 00000001
HostMax:   192.168.1.254        11000000.10101000.00000001. 11111110
Broadcast: 192.168.1.255        11000000.10101000.00000001. 11111111
Hosts/Net: 254                   Class C, Private Internet

## IPv6

IPv6 output uses the same layout as IPv4: Address, Netmask, Wildcard,
Network, HostMin, HostMax, Broadcast and Hosts/Net, with the bits shown
in 16-bit groups and a space marking the network/host boundary.

* The prefix length can be given in CIDR notation (`2001:db8::/48`) or as a
  separate argument (`2001:db8:: 48` or `2001:db8:: /48`). It defaults to `/64`.
* The last line describes the address block (e.g. Global Unicast, Unique Local
  Address, Link-Local Unicast, Multicast, Documentation, 6to4, Teredo,
  IPv4-mapped, Loopback).
* A `/127` is treated as a point-to-point link (RFC 6164): both addresses are
  usable hosts and no Broadcast line is shown. A `/128` is shown as a Hostroute.
* An invalid prefix length is reported as an error (exit code 1).
